durable.evidence: Every mailbox is one Durable Object whose items, head and floor are in its own transactional storage (worker/mailbox.js); test/test-relay-conformance.ps1 reads on from a cursor, and puts the next seq, from a fresh runspace that shares no state with the writer, against a local wrangler dev of the same Worker.

realtime.evidence: A watch is a WebSocket the mailbox's Durable Object holds (hibernating) and answers in the put that fills it; test/test-relay-conformance.ps1 has another runspace put while a watch waits, three rounds, and requires each watch to return within a second of that put.

reach.remote.evidence: The relay is a Worker on a public HTTPS origin, and this adapter reaches it only over HTTP and WebSocket; test/test-relay-conformance.ps1 has a second client, with its own connection, put what the first reads. That run is against a local wrangler dev on 127.0.0.1: the network between two machines is not in it, and the live smoke test after the first deploy is (PR plan item 8).

trim.on.ack.evidence: An ack raises the mailbox's floor and deletes the items through it in one storage transaction, and the head never moves back; test/test-relay-conformance.ps1 reads only what is after the ack and sees the next put numbered after the trimmed ones, also once every item is trimmed.
